headline: Mirpur clashes: Police fire teargas and sound grenades to disperse garment workers
summary: Protests over minimum wage demands enter their fourth day, with clashes erupting in Mirpur-11 as police chase workers who hurled brickbats.
details: RMG workers in Mirpur-11 clashed with police today as they attempted to take to the streets to protest for a higher minimum wage.
Workers walked out of several factories after 10:00 am and gathered in alleys on the western side of Mirpur-11, attempting to reach the main road.
Police, who were on alert, chased the workers, and in response, the protesters hurled brickbats at law enforcement officers.
To disperse the crowd, police fired teargas shells and sound grenades, forcing the workers to retreat from the main road and nearby alleys.
Following the clashes, leaders and activists of Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal and Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal took positions on the road, claiming they were there to prevent sabotage.
Nur Salam, convener of Pallabi Thana Jubo Dal, alleged that Awami League members had infiltrated the workers' movement to create chaos.
Touhidul Arif, deputy commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police, stated that the movement was being driven by 'miscreants with ulterior motives' rather than actual workers.
The protests over minimum wage demands have now entered their fourth consecutive day, causing significant disruption in several industrial areas.
caption:
Teargas and sound grenades in Mirpur! 

Garment workers' protests for higher wages enter their fourth day with violent clashes.

RMG workers in Mirpur-11 clashed with police today as they attempted to take to the streets to protest for a higher minimum wage.

Workers walked out of several factories after 10:00 am and gathered in alleys on the western side of Mirpur-11, attempting to reach the main road.

Police, who were on alert, chased the workers, and in response, the protesters hurled brickbats at law enforcement officers.

To disperse the crowd, police fired teargas shells and sound grenades, forcing the workers to retreat from the main road and nearby alleys.

Following the clashes, leaders and activists of Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal and Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal took positions on the road, claiming they were there to prevent sabotage.

Nur Salam, convener of Pallabi Thana Jubo Dal, alleged that Awami League members had infiltrated the workers' movement to create chaos.

Touhidul Arif, deputy commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police, stated that the movement was being driven by 'miscreants with ulterior motives' rather than actual workers.

The protests over minimum wage demands have now entered their fourth consecutive day, causing significant disruption in several industrial areas.

headline_marked: 2,010 hospitalised as [[6 more die of dengue]] in 24 hours
headline: 2,010 hospitalised as 6 more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: The total death toll for the year has reached 439, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
details: Another six people have died of dengue over the past 24 hours in Bangladesh, while 2,010 patients were hospitalised.
The latest deaths bring this year's total toll to 439, including 20 deaths in the first two days of November.
According to the DGHS, 943 patients were admitted in the Dhaka Division alone between Monday and Tuesday.
Other hospitalisations included 245 in Chattogram, 235 in Khulna, 219 each in Barishal and Rajshahi, 65 in Rangpur, 60 in Mymensingh, and 24 in Sylhet.
A total of 140,909 patients have been admitted nationwide this year, with 134,594 discharged after treatment.
Currently, 5,876 patients remain hospitalised across the country.
The DGHS has maintained records since 2000, noting that 2023 was the worst year on record with 1,705 deaths and 321,179 hospitalisations.
